title: Procurement-ready model availability scorecard and field-probing playbook
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: Enterprise procurement teams need a succinct, quantified view of model availability risk and procurement friction to decide between Reserved (Dedicated) capacity and Hosted fallbacks. Current model-scout notes are fragmented (benchmarks, licensing, cloud region availability, quantization readiness) and not tied to a procurement decision signal.

Objective: Build a lightweight, procurement-ready "model availability scorecard" (MAS) that aggregates supply-side signals into a single actionable score and a short playbook for field probing (commercial + technical) to validate priority risks. The MAS will feed alerts and a dashboard slice in the Signal Hub so PMs and Sales can: 1) prioritize vendor/variant onboarding, 2) estimate fallback costs, 3) trigger pre-commit procurement/provisioning.

Scope:
- Define scorecard inputs and weights (supply capacity, regional latency footprint, license constraints, quantization compatibility, model freshness/deprecation risk, vendor willingness for enterprise SLAs).
- Build a simple ETL that pulls signals from: vendor status pages, cloud capacity telemetry, internal telemetry (latency/fallback rates), Github/model release tags, and partner licensing notes.
- Design a 1-page playbook for field probes (sales + solution engineers) with templated questions, acceptance thresholds, and a short checklist to validate scorecard outputs.
- Prototype a dashboard widget in the Signal Hub and a lightweight alert rule that flags models below threshold for a target region/customer segment.

Out of scope for this ticket: full automation of procurement actions (separate epic), deep legal review of license terms (we will capture high-level friction indicators and route to legal).
acceptance_criteria: Definition: A documented MAS schema with at least 7 signals, weights, and rationale published in Confluence.
Data: ETL prototype that populates the MAS for >= 50 models in our scouting inventory with daily refresh (demo dataset).
Playbook: A one-page field-probing playbook PDF with templated questions and decision thresholds uploaded to Drive.
Dashboard: Signal Hub prototype showing MAS across regions with filtering and an alert rule that triggers on score < 35.
Handoff: Engineering ticket(s) created for productionizing ETL and dashboard, and Sales/SE training checklist created.

risks: Signal noise: Vendor status pages and public indicators are inconsistent; will require manual curation for initial rollout.
Naming collisions: Different sources use different variant names — mapping service required to avoid double-counting capacity.
Legal escalation: Capturing license friction may surface enterprise red-lines that block automated recommendations.
Data freshness: Some signals (contract negotiations) are not machine-readable and will lag; playbook must handle stale cases.
